test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 03 May 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which harvest festival is famously celebrated in Assam?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhogali Bihu**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhogali Bihu:** 

 
 
• This is a **harvest festival celebrated in Assam, a state in northeastern India.** 
 
• Also known as **Magh Bihu**, it marks the end of the harvesting season in the month of Maagha (January-February). 
 
• It involves community feasts and bonfires.
 
• **Bihu **is a set of three important Assamese festivals in the calendar year: **Bhogali (Makar Sankranti), Rongali or Bohag Bihu (Assamese New Year, usually mid-April), and Kongali Bihu (October-November, no specific date).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lohri:**

 
 
• Lohri is a Punjabi festival celebrated primarily by people from the Punjab region of South Asia.
 
• It marks the end of winter and is traditionally associated with the harvest of the rabi crops.
 
• The day is celebrated with a bonfire, singing, dancing, and a feast.
 
 
 
• **Makar Sankranti:**
 
 
• This festival is a pan-Indian solar festival observed in the month of January.
 
• It marks the transition of the sun into the zodiacal sign of Makara (Capricorn) on its celestial path, which is the first change in the zodiac after the winter solstice.
 
• It signifies the arrival of longer days. Makar Sankranti is known by different names in different parts of India and is associated with many customs, which are usually related to the harvest.
 
 
 
• **Onam**:
 
 
• Onam is a harvest festival celebrated in Kerala, a state in South India.
 
• It is the biggest and the most important festival of the state and is celebrated with numerous festivities such as Vallam Kali (boat races), Pulikali (tiger dances), Pookkalam (flower Rangoli), Onathappan (worship), and other celebrations.
